checks.name: real_obj_artifacts

checks.name: layer2_real_mcp_tool_returns
checks.observed: Real MCP initialize (dcc-mcp-zbrush 0.2.32, protocol 2025-06-18), tools/list (32 tools, nextCursor 3332) and 7 real tools/call over /mcp. Only 3 succeeded, all affinity:any catalog/dialog tools: list_skills, load_skill, and zbrush_dialog__get_active_dialog (success=true, bridge_state=ready, zbrush_blocked=false). The 4 main-affinity scene tools genuinely failed, so MCP HTTP scene work is not demonstrated.

checks.name: documented_main_affinity_limitation
checks.observed: 4 real tools/call returned isError=true with THREAD_AFFINITY_UNAVAILABLE. With no host dispatcher attached (host_dispatcher_attached=False) Core correctly refuses declared main-affinity actions. The missing wiring is adapter-side: _executor.py registers only the in-process executor and cli.py's sidecar main loop only sleeps, so no main-thread pump exists. Recorded as an unfixed adapter wiring defect, not a Core design defect; this entry changes neither and does not claim a fix.

checks.name: mcp_http_scene_work_acceptance
checks.observed: NOT CLOSED. 3 of 7 MCP tools/call succeeded, all affinity:any catalog/dialog tools; the 4 main-affinity scene tools returned THREAD_AFFINITY_UNAVAILABLE. The real OBJ import, subdivision, measurement and export were done over Layer 1 socket-bridge JSON-RPC, not MCP tools/call. Socket-bridge success does not establish that MCP HTTP can complete ZBrush scene work, so the requested full MCP capability demonstration remains open. Closing it needs a separately authorized adapter-side dispatcher fix and a fresh live MCP HTTP scene-work run.
